Params: By the time you return to F.O.S. after your mission on the front line is complete, it is already evening.

The rooftop of the school building is particularly stifling. A summer wind carries the scorched smell of asphalt and the thin drone of cicadas. The trees on the street sway, their shadows seemingly hiding time itself.
(Send message) "Sorry I'm late. Where are you?"

You spin around and catch two objects tossed your way almost instinctively: a bottle of iced lemon soda, the same as the one she's drinking, and a white, feathery pendant, the same as the one clipped to her waist.
You crack open the can, and the fizz cuts right through the summer heat.
The white-haired girl walks to the railing nearby and leans against it, putting a deliberate gap between the two of you.
What? You look like you've seen a ghost.
Why are you still in your school uniform?
Isn't it obvious? Because we're still at school.
If anything, you're the one who showed up fully armed in pitch-black armor.
...I came straight from the front lines.
You told me you'd be back last week. Don't tell me you picked up another mission that wasn't even yours.
Yeah. I got stationed in sector A7.
Typical. Always playing the hero, aren't you, 【kuroname】?
I checked. Your name's on the list for the next deployment to A7.
Her smirk fades, and she raises an eyebrow.
There's a lookout that oversees the area if you hold it.
You won't have to fumble around in the dark. It'll be safer.
...Since when do you worry about my safety? Did you forget we tied?
She takes a sulky sip of her lemon soda. Her voice is gentle, but her words are pointed. Still, they are much less aggressive than before.
There's also a field of dandelions there. We can go see it once A7 is safe.
You said it. Don't you dare be late next time.
She stands up and steps a little closer, the tension in her brow finally easing. You did not ask, but she explains herself anyway.
It's cooler on this side. Too much sun where I was standing.
Didn't you have a full schedule today?
Yeah. Kendo lessons for the juniors, my bass lesson, a tour of the virtual planetarium Joanne put together, and the school board's non-negotiable "Glitter Spectacular" fireworks show.
Those things can wait. You, on the other hand, are a lot harder to see.
Six months after your return from the moon, you two have both been folded into the tactical deployment rotations. Taking turns to go on assignments, you have less and less time to meet.
We're graduating next year. This is the last Double Seventh Festival we'll spend at F.O.S.

Small clusters of students are scattered along the crimson boulevard, bursts of their laughter carried through the air. One by one, they walk toward the school gate before disappearing at an unremarkable corner.
So that's why you wanted to meet earlier...
No wonder you wanted to meet early.
Because this is F.O.S. When I was 16, I met a person who picked up my headphones, got into all kinds of trouble with me, and threw me birthday parties.
Because this is F.O.S. Because a lot of good things happened here.
She rests her chin in her hands and sets her empty soda aside, her eyes carrying something unspoken. At her waist, the little white pendant flickers with a faint glow.
I've been meaning to ask... What's the deal with the white pendants?

It's a pair of dandelion pendants... That's your Double Seventh Festival gift. I drew up the patterns and had Joanne make them. She swore they'd glow with our breathing, and the stronger our bond, the brighter they shine.
Do you believe any of that?
Sounds like something off a romance horoscope site.
I don't really believe it, but they do look nicer when they're glowing... Not that Joanne told me how to actually make them glow.
I guess it's the distance. The closer we are, the brighter they get.
She makes a soft, noncommittal sound, and stays right where she is, curled up in the shade.\nSilence settles between you. The cicadas fill it without being asked.
You never answered my question from earlier. You kept staring at me with this look on your face when you showed up. What happened?
...I had a dream on my way back. About the future.
You look exhausted. What did you see?
A lot happened... but you weren't there.
Tell me straight next time, first thing when you see me. I like hearing it.
You're not going to scold me for it?
You're not going to say anything?
You're an idiot. That's just what you are. And an idiot's dream is just a dream.
She ambles over, drapes herself over the railing beside you, and fixes her gaze on the distance. A long silence stretches between you before she speaks again.
Why are you still holding the dandelion pendant? That's not how you wear it.
She does not answer you, sidestepping the question instead. She leans in close and reaches down to fasten the little white pendant to your waist.
Her silver hair glistens in the light, while the red tips burn alongside the setting sun like a dream.
This thing just isn't shiny enough.
Beneath the blazing sun, the little dandelion pendant looks dull. She stares at it, her lips pressed into a small, dissatisfied pout.
I wouldn't care any other day, but today is our last Double Seventh Festival in F.O.S.

The last of the sunset traces her silhouette in deep crimson. The wind lifts her silver hair, and a few stray strands tickle your cheek. Her breath brushes against your face, faint and sweet like lemon soda.
...Come closer, like when we were back on the moon. Let them shine a little brighter.

Facing each other's blinking charms, you move closer until your foreheads touch, and both pendants blaze to life. They glow and dim unevenly at first, but the pulses slowly align, until there is no telling one from the other.
The fading sunset, her smile, her tenderness and resolve... all of it comes down at once, burning so bright it feels like it might leave a mark on your cheek.
If that dream of yours ever comes true...
Why don't you prove me wrong?
I was joking. Don't tell me you took it seriously.
But if you were being honest...
The honest answer is that you're not getting away from me.
The honest answer is that you owe me. You haven't kept a single promise.
The honest answer is that the back seat of my bike has been empty for a long time now, because someone is always too busy to show up.
The honest answer is that I'm not going anywhere. I'll always be there with you.

She stands with one hand on her hip, her silver hair fluttering wildly in the light. The promises of the young are fearless things, blind to the turning of the stars, the gaze of the world, or the designs of fate.
Their affection is reckless and unashamed, playful and all-encompassing... It is a feeling only the midsummer knows: the beautiful illusion that it will never end.

No grand destiny. No sweeping joy and sorrow stretched across endless time. A galaxy spanning thousands of light-years. A planet barely 12000 kilometers wide. A school just 4 years old. A rooftop no more than 50 paces across—
<size=50>She has tried so hard to hold on to that summer.</size>

Alpha turns the glistening memory over in her mind. Her hand drifts to her waist, but there is nothing there. The dandelion pendant and the world it came from are both gone, left behind on the road that no longer exists.

Outside the window, a sea of dandelions drifts quietly in the garden. On the other side of the world, there is a sea she once tended herself. So her gaze passes through the garden and comes to rest somewhere far away.

By the time you return to the old F.O.S. after your mission on the front line is complete, it is already evening. The rooftop of the old building is now a ruin. You search, but there is no one there, just like back then.
A lock of silver-white hair from your memory flashes and vanishes. The drone of cicadas, the sweetness of lemon soda, the girl's smile, the untroubled dreams... All of it feels like a distant mirage.

Coming back to your senses, you find the hills close enough to touch from the rooftop's edge. A patch of dandelions blooms nearby, bright and white, every one of them carefully tended... by someone who never came.
The honest answer is that I'm not going anywhere. I'll always be there with you.

From the Ascendant's quarters, Alpha watches in silence as 【kuroname】 climbs alone to the crumbling rooftop and stands there with unmistakable loss. And that fills her with something that feels like joy.

But then 【kuroname】 looks up with a warm and distant gaze, and she pauses. The lips move without a sound, just like that moment on the moon long ago when the comms were cut, and words were spoken silently through their visors.
(Wherever you are... I hope you're happy.)
(No matter how far you go... you will always be... where I belong.)
"Wherever you are... I hope you're happy."
"You will always be... where I belong."
...I'd repeat those words to you too. Happy Double Seventh Festival, 【kuroname】.

Alpha does not attend the date on the first Double Seventh Festival after her return from the Fog. But she knows the promises made are indelible. No matter the distance, those words will always hold her tired soul.
Outside the window, the sun sinks below the horizon, and night settles in. Dandelion seeds catch the soft, pale moonlight, drifting weightlessly between two ends of the world.
